title: One task, end to end: a rename in the extension
note: A routine rename, traced through the shared server, the retained loop, the agent's ruleset and the permission gate - the same path a CLI run takes, minus the webview.
example_input: Rename the session-host routes and update their callers.

steps.title: A prompt in the sidebar
steps.narrative: The person types a task in the VS Code sidebar: rename the session-host routes and update their callers. The webview does not host a loop - it sends the prompt to the one shared kilo serve backend the extension spawned for the sidebar, editor tabs and Agent Manager alike.
steps.representation:
webview --HTTP--> kilo serve (shared backend)
  prompt: "rename the session-host routes..."
  session: ses_...  agent: code

modules.label: serve.ts:7 - starts a headless kilo server

steps.title: The server opens the session step
steps.narrative: The server loads (or creates) the session, resolves its agent - code, the default primary - and hands the prompt to SessionPrompt. Session state, not webview state, is the record: the transcript lives in the server's store.

steps.title: The loop assembles and streams
steps.narrative: The retained loop begins: while(true). Step one assembles the messages - system prompt for the code agent, the project's AGENTS.md instructions, the stored history - and streams one model call through the processor. The reply asks to read two files and edit one.
steps.representation:
while (true) {          // prompt.ts:1555
  msgs = system + instructions + history
  stream(model) -> parts + tool calls
}

steps.title: The agent profile shapes the step
steps.narrative: Everything about this step comes from the agent definition: the code agent's prompt, its model, and its permission ruleset - base defaults merged with the agent's rules and the user's config by patchAgents and the agent builder. In plan, the same edit below would be denied outright.
steps.representation:
agent code = { prompt, model,
  permission: merge(defaults, agent, user) }

modules.label: index.ts:485 - patchAgents: Kilo's agent patch layer
agent.ts:169 - the build agent (renamed to code)

steps.title: The permission gate
steps.narrative: Before the edit runs, the engine evaluates it: wildcard match over the merged ruleset, last match wins. Reads of the two source files are allowed; the edit matches no allow rule, so the default applies - ask. The person answers once. (An .env read would also have asked: the defaults carve secrets out of the read allow.)
steps.representation:
evaluate("edit", path, rulesets)
  last matching rule -> allow | ask | deny
  no match -> ask  => person replies: once

modules.label: index.ts:102 - evaluate: last matching rule wins

steps.title: Tools execute; results append
steps.narrative: Approved calls run: the reads, then the edit. Tool results are appended as message parts, and the snapshot service records the worktree state for this step - which is what will make this message a revert point later.
steps.representation:
read a.ts -> ok    read b.ts -> ok
edit routes.ts -> applied
snapshot: patch part stored on the message

modules.label: revert.ts - revert walks message patch parts

steps.title: The next step goes to the model
steps.narrative: The loop iterates: history plus tool results go back to the provider layer - a catalog model, or the Kilo Gateway when the session uses a Kilo account. The model updates the callers and, satisfied, answers with text and no tool calls.
steps.representation:
step 2: stream(model, history + results)
  -> text, no tool calls => loop exits

steps.title: The turn closes; context is kept honest
steps.narrative: The run finishes. Had the history overflowed the model's usable context (limit minus a reserved buffer capped at 20,000 tokens), compaction would have summarized the older turns mid-loop. At turn close, project memory captures what is worth keeping for the next session; the recall tool can search this transcript later.
steps.representation:
tokens < usable(context, reserved<=20k)
  -> no compaction this turn
memory: capture at turn close; recall later
